newsitem.title: USA: Two tried to extort money from Cosby - prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Two tried to extort money from Cosby - prosecutor.

text.p: A Los Angeles woman and an alleged accomplice have been arrested on charges of attempting to extort $40 million from entertainer Bill Cosby in exchange for not telling the media she was his illegitimate daughter, law enforcement officials said on Monday.
CBS news and ABC news reported that a Cosby spokesman vehemently denied Jackson was Cosby's daughter.

There is no evidence the blackmail attempt was related to the murder last week of Cosby's only son, Ennis, Mary Jo White, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, said in a prepared statement.

Autumn Jackson, 22, and Jose Medina, 51, were arrested on Saturday after they signed an agreement not to sell the story to tabloid newspapers in an office of a "representative" of the actor, said Joseph Valiquette, a spokesman for the New York FBI office.
The unnamed representative had gone to the FBI after the demands were made, he said.

Jackson and Medina were scheduled to make an appearance in U.S. District Court on Tuesday, Valiquette said. They both face possible two-year jail sentences and $250,000 fines for extortion and five years in prison and $250,000 in fines for conspiracy, he said.
Originally Jackson sought $40 million, Valiquette said, but by Saturday she had settled for $18 million for herself and $6 million for Medina.
How Medina fit into the scheme or was related to Jackson was unclear, Valiquette said.
Valiquette said it was unclear when the extortion plot began, but court documents related to the case said the Cosby family had paid educational expenses for the woman for "several years."
The FBI said it recorded three conversations between the representative and Jackson in which she said she was willing to accept the money "to end everything."
